name: pulmonary nodule overview
title: Pulmonary nodule and mass decision chart: one nodule is followed by size and malignancy risk (Fleischner) and sent on to a lung cancer workup when large, high risk or a mass; multiple nodules are benign inflammatory or infectious causes or metastases; columns give clues, workup and management

root.title: Lung opacity: NODULE (< 3 cm) or MASS (> 3 cm)? ONE or MANY?
lines: usually found by chance on imaging, in someone with no symptoms

groups.title: ONE nodule: SIZE + RISK decide
lines: HIGH RISK: older, smoker, emphysema, family history
nodule: bigger, SPICULATED, UPPER lobe, part-solid

tiers.title: Follow-up CT by size (Fleischner)
lines: • ≤ 5 mm: none if LOW risk · optional CT at 12 months if HIGH
• 6–8 mm: CT at 6–12 months, then 18–24 months
• ≥ 8 mm: consider CT at 3 months, positron emission tomography (PET)/CT or BIOPSY

head: h
Benign solitary nodule
more common overall
inv: Watch with CT at the intervals above
tx: Low risk, ≤ 5 mm: no routine follow-up

head: h
Lung cancer
non-small cell (adenocarcinoma #1) or small cell
squamous and small cell sit CENTRALLY
pres: • or cough, dyspnea, hemoptysis, chest pain
• superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction, Pancoast tumour
inv: finds unsuspected metastases in up to 30%
3 · BIOPSY: stage + diagnosis in ONE procedure
tx: radiation if not a surgical candidate

head: h
Multiple nodules
tx: Pleural or pericardial EFFUSION = STAGE IV
